key_insight: The paper formalizes temporally sparse 4D semantic instance segmentation and shows how to maintain consistent object identities across intermittently captured, evolving indoor 3D scans by combining per-scan segmentation with temporal association across unobserved gaps.
problem_solved: How to jointly segment, identify, and temporally associate object instances in indoor 3D scenes when scans are captured intermittently and objects may move, appear, or disappear between observations.
method: Define the temporally sparse 4D SIS task and provide a benchmark/dataset and evaluation protocol (ReScene4D) targeting long gaps and unobserved changes.
Produce per-scan 3D semantic instance segmentations and learn identity-aware embeddings that enable robust instance matching across scans using geometric and appearance cues.
Introduce temporal-association strategies and metrics to evaluate and enforce identity consistency over time despite intermittent observations and occlusions.
impact: Enables robust long-term scene understanding for robotics, AR, and monitoring systems by ensuring persistent instance identities across sparse 3D captures; provides a standardized benchmark to drive progress in temporally consistent 3D perception.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing intermittent 3D scans with the same objects tracked and color-coded instance IDs across time (including moved/removed/appeared objects).
Before/after 3D scene renderings that highlight consistent instance labels despite object movement or disappearance.
Pipeline diagram: per-scan 3D segmentation -> identity embedding extraction -> cross-scan matching/association.
Benchmark bar chart or radar chart comparing temporal-consistency metrics (identity F1, association accuracy) across methods.
paper_title: ReScene4D: Temporally Consistent Semantic Instance Segmentation of Evolving Indoor 3D Scenes
paper_authors: Emily Steiner, Jianhao Zheng, Henry Howard-Jenkins, Chris Xie, Iro Armeni
